titleText.es: Las epidemias de gripe azotan con más fuerza a los adultos jóvenes porque sus sistemas inmunitarios reaccionan con más fuerza, así que para permanecer sanos tenéis que pasaros las próximas semanas borrachos y privados de sueño.
titleText.en: Flu epidemics hit young adults harder because their immune systems react more strongly, so to stay healthy you all have to spend the next few weeks drunk and sleep-deprived.
titleText.noteEn: This translates the Spanish archive text. The official English title text adds that this behavior is meant to keep the immune system ‘suppressed’; that final purpose is absent from the Spanish archive. The joke reverses ordinary health advice by treating a weakened immune response as protection.

cardDefinitions.answerEn: uninformed; based on poor information (masculine singular)

cardDefinitions.noteEn: Porcina describes something related to pigs. Its -a ending matches a feminine singular noun such as gripe.

example.es: La granja aplica controles de sanidad porcina.
example.en: The farm applies swine-health controls.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: Cerdo can name the animal or its meat. This card is for the food meaning.

example.es: No como cerdo.
example.en: I do not eat pork.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: This card is for the animal, not pork as food.

example.es: El cerdo duerme en el establo.
example.en: The pig sleeps in the barn.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: Americana ordinarily means ‘American’ in the feminine singular. In Spain, the fixed name cinta americana refers to strong cloth-backed duct tape.

example.es: Necesito cinta americana para arreglarlo.
example.en: I need duct tape to fix it.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: Contra can introduce the danger that a barrier, medicine, or precaution is meant to stop.

example.es: Esta crema protege contra el sol.
example.en: This cream protects against the sun.

cardDefinitions.answerEn: to get it; to obtain it
cardDefinitions.noteEn: Conseguir is the unchanged dictionary form ‘to get.’ La is attached to its end and replaces one feminine thing.

example.es: Quiero conseguirla hoy.
example.en: I want to get it today.

cardDefinitions.answerEn: to go out; to go outside
before; until, after an amount of remaining time
cardDefinitions.noteEn: After an expression such as queda tiempo, para que can introduce the later event that the remaining time leads up to. It does not express a desired purpose in this use.

example.es: Queda una hora para que empiece la película.
example.en: There is one hour left until the film starts.

cardDefinitions.answerEn: no separate English word; completes the time connector after para
cardDefinitions.noteEn: Here que joins para to a full later event with its own changed verb.

example.es: Faltan dos días para que llegue Marta.
example.en: There are two days left until Marta arrives.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: Caído is the completed-action form of caer, ‘to fall.’

example.es: El vaso se ha caído.
example.en: The glass has fallen.

cardDefinitions.answerEn: sounds; seems (before a comparison with a)
cardDefinitions.noteEn: A form of sonar followed by a can compare the impression something gives with another thing.

example.es: Eso suena a excusa.
example.en: That sounds like an excuse.

cardDefinitions.answerEn: like; required after sonar before the comparison
cardDefinitions.noteEn: In sonar a algo, the preposition a links the impression to what it resembles.

example.es: La historia suena a broma.
example.en: The story sounds like a joke.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: Vinculadas describes more than one thing named by a feminine noun. The usual link to the related thing is a.

example.es: Las cuentas están vinculadas al mismo correo.
example.en: The accounts are linked to the same email address.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: Autista has the same singular form with masculine and feminine nouns.

example.es: Es una estudiante autista.
example.en: She is an autistic student.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: Proteger is the unchanged dictionary form ‘to protect.’ Me attaches to its end and makes the speaker the person protected.

example.es: Uso guantes para protegerme.
example.en: I use gloves to protect myself.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: Gripe means flu. Porcina means related to pigs and takes its feminine singular form to match the feminine noun gripe.

example.es: El hospital confirmó un caso de gripe porcina.
example.en: The hospital confirmed a case of swine flu.

cardDefinitions.questionEn: What does cinta americana name in Spain?
cardDefinitions.noteEn: This is a fixed regional name for strong cloth-backed adhesive tape. Other places may prefer cinta adhesiva or cinta de tela.

example.es: Cierra la caja con cinta americana.
example.en: Seal the box with duct tape.

cardDefinitions.questionEn: How do you say how much time someone has left?
cardDefinitions.answerEn: Put me, te, le, nos, os, or les before quedar, and make quedar singular or plural to match the time amount that remains.
cardDefinitions.noteEn: Spanish presents the time as remaining to the person. Use queda with one remaining unit and quedan with plural units: me queda una hora, but me quedan dos horas. The small word before quedar identifies who has that time left. You may add a + a name or person to clarify who: A Marta le quedan dos horas.

example.es: A Marta le quedan dos horas.
example.en: Marta has two hours left.

cardDefinitions.promptEs: tiempo restante + para que + evento futuro
cardDefinitions.questionEn: How do you name the later event that a remaining amount of time leads up to?
cardDefinitions.answerEn: After the remaining-time expression, use para que and put the later event's verb in its special not-yet-a-fact form.
cardDefinitions.noteEn: That special form is called the subjunctive. It appears because the later event is still ahead: ordinary empieza becomes empiece, and ordinary llega becomes llegue. In this time construction, para que means that the stated time remains before or until the event; it is not giving a purpose.

example.es: Quedan dos horas para que empiece el partido.
example.en: There are two hours left until the match starts.

cardDefinitions.questionEn: How do you say that something sounds like something else?
cardDefinitions.answerEn: Use a form of sonar, then a, then the thing it resembles.
cardDefinitions.noteEn: Sonar changes to match the person or thing producing the impression and the time: suena for one present thing, suenan for several. The word a stays unchanged before the comparison.

example.es: Ese plan suena a desastre.
example.en: That plan sounds like a disaster.

cardDefinitions.questionEn: How do you say that one thing is linked to another?
cardDefinitions.answerEn: Use a form of estar, then vinculado changed to match the linked thing, then a before the related thing.
cardDefinitions.noteEn: Estar changes to match the linked person or thing and the time: está for one present item and están for several. Vinculada describes one feminine-noun item, vinculados several masculine or mixed items, and vinculadas several feminine-noun items. The linking word a stays unchanged, but it combines with el as al.

example.es: La cuenta está vinculada al teléfono.
example.en: The account is linked to the phone.

cardDefinitions.promptEs: gripe porcina · pánico desinformado en Twitter
cardDefinitions.answerEn: The 2009 H1N1 outbreak was widely called ‘swine flu.’ Twitter's then-new real-time search made it easy to watch rumors, fear, and wildly mistaken self-diagnoses spread alongside genuine news.
cardDefinitions.noteEn: The strip turns a live search page into a rapid sample of online panic: unrelated injuries, conspiracy claims, and impossible precautions are all attributed to the same outbreak.

cardDefinitions.answerEn: The claim that vaccines cause autism is false. Extensive research across large populations has found that vaccines do not cause autism.
cardDefinitions.noteEn: The comic places that false claim inside a stream of absurd health misinformation. The later action toward an autistic child extends the joke by showing a dangerous conclusion drawn from the same false premise.
